items.label: NAD+ precursors (NR/NMN/niacin) x primary mitochondrial diseases
items.rationale: Best human evidence is a one-day double-blind phase-1 CMA (NR/NMN) study showing NAD+ biomarker elevation only, no clinical endpoints (37271226), a 28-person cohort with in-vitro myotube NAD+/respiration/ATP benefits that were not significant (40846977), and a single-patient niacin case report that did not stop disease progression despite a favorable metabolomics shift (39173541). Preclinical signal is mixed: NR improved contractility and stress markers but aggravated erythrocyte maturation defects, worsening anemia (42669151). Reviews support only NAD+ homeostasis, not outcomes (42489969, 41516357). Pipeline: registered phase-1 NR trial (NCT07344636) and a planned NR+exercise trial (NCT04907110), neither with posted results, so they raise pipeline_momentum only. No disease-modifying standard exists (supportive care only), so unmet need is maximal; oral small molecules with short-term human tolerability (37271226) but an anemia safety signal (42669151) temper translatability.

items.label: Urolithin A x chronic heart failure
items.rationale: Two independent preclinical studies with consistent benefit: significant improvements in diastolic function, attenuation of remodeling, and enhanced relaxation/contraction kinetics in human EHT (42616901), plus non-significant alleviation of diastolic dysfunction, hypertrophy and fibrosis with restored mitophagic flux in an HFpEF mouse model (42432192). No human efficacy data and no registered CHF trial for urolithin A in this set, so pipeline is weak. Guideline-directed medical therapy is robust (SoC map), but HFpEF has few disease-modifying options, giving moderate unmet need. Oral small molecule; human feasibility supported by PK/bioavailability trials (NCT07231848, NCT07517913) and a frailty RCT (NCT06556706; no results) in the same molecule, but not in CHF.

items.label: NAD+ precursors (NR/NMN) x chronic heart failure
items.rationale: Only human data is a single-arm phase-1 NR trial (n=30): safe and well tolerated, whole-blood NAD+ approximately doubled, PBMC basal/maximal respiration increased with significant NAD+ correlations, NLRP3 expression decreased (36644285) - all surrogates, no control arm, no patient-important endpoints. The 'meta'-tiered record is a review stating clinical trials are ongoing, not a pooled effect estimate (42047243); the stable-isotope NR record is a preclinical NMR probe method, not efficacy (42122439). Robust GDMT (ACEi/ARB/ARNI, beta-blockers, MRA, SGLT2i per SoC map) limits unmet need. Oral small molecule with demonstrated human tolerability (36644285) supports translatability.

items.label: NMN x sepsis-induced acute kidney injury
items.rationale: Randomized animal study with significant reductions in tubular damage, glomerular congestion, inflammatory infiltration and histopathological score (42585475) - a strong, consistent preclinical direction, but a single study with no human data or trials, so this is a thin evidence base: raw weighted total 4.1 is capped at 4.0. AKI management is largely supportive with few disease-modifying options, so unmet need is high. Oral/infusible small molecule, but no human safety data in sepsis-AKI and no delivery/schedule evidence.

items.label: PQQ x glaucoma
items.rationale: Single narrative review (thin evidence base) with consistent positive preclinical claims - ATP preservation under mitochondrial stress, RGC density protection, NAD+ elevation along the visual pathway - plus a PQQ-containing combination RCT reported to show functional improvement that cannot be tiered rct or verified without the primary report (42653764). No registered trials in this set. IOP-lowering drugs and surgery exist but no neuroprotective standard, giving moderate unmet need. Oral small molecule with an established safety record supports translatability.

items.label: Nicotinamide riboside chloride (NRC) x alcohol-induced neuronal damage
items.rationale: Single preclinical study (thin evidence base): NRC significantly improved alcohol-related cognitive impairment and neuroinflammation and restored mitochondrial homeostasis via UPRmt and FUNDC1-dependent mitophagy (42327979). Direction is positive and partly significant, but entirely preclinical with no human data, no trials, and no dosing/safety information, so translatability and pipeline are low. Limited disease-modifying therapy for alcohol-related neurocognitive injury supports unmet need (judged; disease not in SoC map).

items.label: Restorin NR (NR fumarate) x aging
items.rationale: Single preclinical 3-arm comparison in aged mice (thin evidence base): Restorin NR produced significantly higher circulating NAD+ at 1 mmol/kg/day, and a low dose was NAD+-equivalent to NR chloride or NMN (42582917) - a biomarker-only effect with no functional or clinical readout. No trials or human data. 'Aging' is not a disease with a standard therapy, so unmet need is scored high but is judgmental (not in SoC map). Oral crystalline small molecule, but long-term safety/dosing unproven.

items.label: NR x peripheral artery disease
items.rationale: One registered phase-3 RCT (n=250) with patient-important endpoints - 6-minute walk distance, WIQ, PROMIS Mobility, MRI calf perfusion - but no posted results (NCT07782671). Per rubric, registry-only evidence raises pipeline_momentum only and never evidence_quality or effect_direction, which therefore stay at unknown/neutral. Thin single-record evidence base (cap 4; not binding, raw total 3.5). PAD has established revascularization, exercise and antithrombotic standards, so unmet need is moderate (judged; not in SoC map). Oral NR, an established small molecule, supports translatability.

items.label: Urolithin A (Mitopure) x frailty in older adults
items.rationale: Single registered, placebo-controlled pilot RCT (n=26) assessing muscle mitochondrial quality with no results posted (NCT06556706) - registry-only, so it contributes to pipeline_momentum only. Thin single-record evidence base. No disease-modifying frailty therapy exists, so unmet need is high (judged; not in SoC map). Oral Mitopure formulation with ongoing human trials supports reasonable translatability.

items.label: Urolithin A PK/delivery (primary mitochondrial diseases + unassigned PK)
items.rationale: Two pharmacokinetic records with no efficacy endpoints: urolithin A CSF kinetics in primary mitochondrial diseases (NCT07517913) and a single-dose randomized bioavailability study of UA formulations with unassigned disease (NCT07231848). No effect_direction signal exists; the CSF data partially address the unresolved CNS-delivery question for mito-targeted drugs. Primary MTD has no disease-modifying standard (SoC map), so unmet need is maximal. Merged into one direction (see caveats); counted as active pipeline development without any efficacy evidence.

items.label: Natural bioactive compounds x myocardial infarction
items.rationale: Single meta-analytic record (thin evidence base) that only 'links' nature-derived bioactives (dietary fibers, polyphenols) to cardiac repair without a quantified pooled effect on patient-important outcomes (41927585) - effect direction is positive but unproven. No registered trials. Post-MI care (reperfusion, secondary prevention) is established, though residual remodeling risk persists, so unmet need is moderate (judged; not in SoC map). Oral dietary compounds with good safety, but no defined pharmaceutical formulation or dosing.

items.label: Urolithin A x Parkinson's disease
items.rationale: Single review (thin evidence base) describing the UA/AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1alpha/Parkin/mitophagy pathway as disrupted in AD and PD, with direction explicitly unclear (42570712) - mechanistic rationale only, no efficacy data, no trials for UA in PD in this set. PD has symptomatic but no disease-modifying standard therapy, so unmet need is high. Oral small molecule with human trials in other indications supports translatability.

items.label: NR x acute myeloid leukaemia
items.rationale: Single review (thin evidence base) claiming selective leukaemic cell death with NAD supplementation, with no primary data, no patient-level outcomes and no trials (42514364). AML has aggressive standard care (chemotherapy, immunotherapy, stem-cell transplant) with meaningful response rates, so unmet need is moderate (judged; not in SoC map). Achieving therapeutic intracellular NAD+ in the myeloid compartment at safe NR doses is unresolved, so translatability is low.

items.label: Urolithin A/B x skeletal muscle health
items.rationale: Single in-vitro transcriptomics study (thin evidence base): UA and UB significantly modulated gene expression (1918 and 339 genes) and UA affected NOTCH1/PANX1/FGF9, but all outcomes are direction-unclear with no functional muscle readouts (42773997). 'Muscle health' is not a defined disease with standard therapy, so unmet need is scored from judgment (not in SoC map). No human data or trials for this indication; preclinical-only translatability.

items.label: NAD+ precursors x musculoskeletal diseases
items.rationale: Single review (thin evidence base) describing mitochondria-targeted therapies including NAD+ boosters as a 'promising foundation' with direction explicitly unclear (42727834) - no efficacy data, no trials. Musculoskeletal 'diseases' is a heterogeneous umbrella with established treatments for many conditions, so unmet need is moderate at best (judged; not in SoC map). Oral small-molecule class, but no indication-specific safety or dosing evidence.

items.label: Mitophagy interventions x chronic heart failure
items.rationale: Single review (thin evidence base) describing mitophagy as a context-dependent regulator of cardiac metabolic reprogramming (FAO, glycolysis, OXPHOS) with no directional therapeutic claim (42746169) - rationale-level only. No trials. Robust GDMT per the SoC map leaves little unmet need for a general mitophagy strategy. The intervention class spans pharmacological, substrate-based and exercise modalities, so a single therapeutic is not defined.

items.label: Gut-derived metabolites (SCFA/I3P; NAD+/SIRT3 signaling) x chronic heart failure
items.rationale: Single meta-analytic synthesis (thin evidence base) that associates the gut-metabolite/NAD+-SIRT3 axis with myocardial fibrosis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and adverse outcomes - a harmful/neutral signal (42609595) - and cautions it 'should not be interpreted as uniformly protective'. No therapeutic is defined (endogenous metabolites), no trials, and robust GDMT exists (SoC map). Effect_direction scored 0 for the adverse association.

outsiders: Gut-derived metabolites (SCFA/I3P; NAD+/SIRT3) x chronic heart failure (1.2): the only record is a synthesis associating this axis with myocardial fibrosis, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and adverse outcomes, with no therapeutic defined (42609595).
Mitophagy interventions x chronic heart failure (1.6): a single review describing mitophagy as context-dependent with no directional therapeutic claim and no trials (42746169).
NAD+ precursors x musculoskeletal diseases (2.1): a single review at 'promising foundation' level with explicitly unclear direction and no trials (42727834).
Urolithin A/B x skeletal muscle health (2.6): a single in-vitro transcriptomics study with direction-unclear gene modulation and no functional or human data (42773997).
caveats: No convincing leaders yet: the top direction (NAD+ precursors x primary mitochondrial diseases, 5.1) is below the 6.0 leader threshold; no direction has posted phase-2/3 efficacy results.

No direction in this set has posted clinical results. All registered trials (NCT07782671, NCT07344636, NCT04907110, NCT06556706, NCT07231848, NCT07517913) are registry-only and were counted toward pipeline_momentum only, never toward evidence_quality or effect_direction, per rubric rule 3.

13 of 17 directions rest on a single ref_id and are flagged 'thin evidence base' (total capped at 4): NRC x alcohol neurodegeneration; Restorin NR x aging; NR x PAD; UA x frailty; bioactives x MI; UA x PD; NR x AML; UA/B x muscle health; NAD+ x MSK; mitophagy x CHF; gut metabolites x CHF; NMN x sepsis-AKI (cap binding: 4.1 -> 4.0); PQQ x glaucoma (cap non-binding at exactly 4.0).

No record contains a standard-of-care comparator arm (GDMT for CHF, idebenone for LhON, supportive care for primary MTD), so all effect_direction scores are relative to placebo/vehicle only and the central question (mito therapy vs standard care) is unanswered (36644285, 39173541, 42432192).

Outcomes are predominantly surrogates (circulating NAD+, PBMC respiration, gene expression, histopathology scores, PK parameters) rather than patient-important endpoints, which caps evidence_quality across the board; the PQQ x glaucoma RCT claim cannot be verified without the primary report (42653764).

unmet_need for diseases outside the SoC map (PAD, frailty, PD, MI, AML, sepsis-AKI, glaucoma, aging, alcohol neurodegeneration, muscle health, MSK) is judged on general knowledge and is flagged as such in the relevant rationales.

NCT07231848 (disease recorded as 'unclear') and NCT07517913 (primary MTD, CSF PK) were merged into one urolithin A PK/delivery direction; scored separately, each would be a thin single-study direction. NCT04907110 (NR + exercise co-intervention) was folded into the NAD+ precursor x primary MTD direction.

The negative-phase-3 cap on effect_direction (max 3) is not triggered: no negative phase-3 result exists in this set, and the ongoing phase-3 NR x PAD trial has no posted results, so it was scored as unknown, not negative (NCT07782671).

Mixed preclinical signals temper class-level optimism: NR aggravated erythrocyte maturation and worsened anemia (42669151), niacin failed to stop disease progression (39173541), gut-metabolite NAD+/SIRT3 signaling was associated with adverse outcomes (42609595), and mitophagy is context-dependent rather than uniformly protective (42746169).
